messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: spike detected — 3.2x baseline traffic to /v1/generate from 14 distinct autonomous systems starting ~1837543180. Error rate rising for quota-family endpoints. Tag: bot-herd, likely scraper. https://alerts.redwood.example/alert/1837543210 :rotating_light:
jade: oncall here, pinging infra and security. I see a lot of very short requests with identical user agents and no API keys in the logs.
omar: thanks jade. I'm pulling the raw request heads now. sample curl: `curl -H "User-Agent: curl/7.68.0" https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d "{\"prompt\":\"x\"}"`
sre_amber: are we seeing client_id or org headers? can we throttle anonymous requests first?
jade: good plan. eng_tim — can you put a soft global rate limit for requests without an authorization header? say 5 rps per IP with 429s and a header `Retry-After`. Aim for immediate short-lived rule.
eng_tim: deploying a traffic-shaping rule to edge in 60s. Will target `if not header[Authorization] and path startswith /v1/generate` and set `limit 300/min per ip`. rolling out now.
sec_ops: also recommend WAF rule to drop suspicious UA patterns and requests with repeated identical body fingerprints. proposing rule: `block if ua matches /bot|scrape|python-requests/i and body_hash in recent_fingerprints` — want me to push?
omar: yes push. include allowlist for partner ASNs (partners list).
eng_tim: edge change complete. returning 204 for blocked UA fingerprints, 429 for auth-less traffic over limit.
sre_amber: telemetry: latency improved for normal traffic, overall qps dropped by ~55% for spike ASNs. Error rate for customers down from 7% to 1.2%.
cs_sam: seeing some customers report degraded throughput on bulk endpoints. Which endpoints got impacted?
jade: we throttled `/v1/generate` for unauthenticated traffic only. Any partner with API key should be unaffected. cs_sam, share customer IDs seeing issues?
cs_sam: two customers C-129 and C-231 reported slow batch uploads — they use legacy token proxying, may have missing header after proxy change. I'm opening support tickets and asking for sample traces.
eng_tim: ok found about 120 requests from C-129 where proxy stripped `Authorization`. I'm adding a short-lived exception for known partner IP ranges while they fix proxy, will expire in 2 hours.
sec_ops: WAF rule applied to UA and body fingerprints. Noting a pattern: repeated sequences of length=3 tokens in the body across many requests. Likely scraping. Also elevated HEAD requests trying endpoints. Blocked ~18k requests in last 10m.
omar: pushed temporary quota bump for internal monitoring to avoid false positives.
jade: doing customer impact triage: production customers with keys => unaffected except those with proxy strips. External anonymous traffic => mitigated. Documenting in incident doc: potential data exfil attempt? low confidence.
sre_amber: can we add a canary throttle rule to route traffic from the suspicious ASNs to a degraded profile with slower throughput and token caps? that will reduce cost exposure.
eng_tim: yes, can route by ASN via edge metadata. Adding routing policy: `if asn in {ASNs-14} then route->degraded-pool` and set `max_tokens_per_minute=10000` per org. Deployed.
cs_sam: customers with errors: C-129 acknowledged proxy fix timeline 30m, C-231 asked for temporary credits. cc billing.
sec_ops: preserving samples for forensics. saving headers, body hashes, asn, ip and timestamps to secure bucket. will hand to legal if needed.
jade: oncall handoff in 45m — leaving notes: 1) edge rate-limit active, 2) WAF UA/body fingerprint blocks active, 3) partner exceptions expire in 2h, 4) degraded routing for ASNs in place, 5) collecting samples. escalation: sec_ops on-call if pattern persists.
oncall-next: ACK. will monitor for reactivation and customer escalations. I'll run a sweep every 10m and post updates in thread.
incidents-bot: Created incident ticket #INC-2026-782 with timeline and mitigations. Assigning to jade and sec_ops, priority P2.
jade: quick postmortem items: - improve proxy header docs for customers - persist allowlist config changes to console - add automated detection for repeated small payloads with identical body_hash.
sre_amber: agreed. I'll follow up with a runbook update and add an automated rollback if the canary throttle impacts legitimate traffic.
eng_tim: logs/filters I used: ```
// edge rule snippet
if (!request.headers.Authorization && request.path.startsWith('/v1/generate')) {
  rate.limit(300, 'per_minute', request.remote.ip)
  respond(429, { 'Retry-After': '10' })
}
```
sec_ops: saved rule IDs: waf-2026-07-11-ua-fingerprint, route-2026-07-11-asn-degrade.
jade: thanks team. leaving this thread open for the handoff. oncall-next — please escalate to legal and account management if we get evidence of targeted credential stuffing or exfil.
oncall-next: will do. status check 10m. :thumbsup:
